create-payment.why: Checkout completing is the only way a job reaches escrow

release-payout.why: A real Stripe transfer row is written per release

process-scheduled-payouts.why: The cron stamps its own initiator, so admin rows do not count as proof

auto-release-payment.why: Same table, distinguished by initiator; filters is_seed=false so seed rows can never prove it

execute-dispute-split.why: A split writes exactly one claim row per settlement

auto-resolve-disputes.observable: disputes.status='decided' AND decided_by IS NULL AND decision_text LIKE 'Auto-resolved by platform policy%' (plus the orphan-sweep text 'Closed by the auto-resolve sweep')
auto-resolve-disputes.why: Guess wrong twice: disputes has no 'resolved' status (live values are open/withdrawn/decided), and 'no admin actor' alone does NOT isolate the auto path - 5 of the 8 rows are user WITHDRAWALS that also carry decided_by IS NULL. The auto path IS distinguishable, by the decision_text it writes (index.ts:610) alongside decided_by=null in settle_dispute_record. Measured 2026-09-22 on prod, all 8 dispute rows read: exactly ONE matches (9756a585, decided 2026-09-16 06:21Z, execution_status='executed') and its job is is_seed=true, so the auto path has run but only on a fixture. dispute_settlement_claims still 0. Cron alive: 30 retained runs, all succeeded, last 2026-09-22 12:21Z

auto-tip-charge.why: Each charged tip writes a row

instant-payout.why: One row per instant payout requested

cash-out-credits.why: Cashing out moves credit to a real transfer

create-gift-card-checkout.why: A purchase writes the card row

create-boost-payment.why: Guess right. Measured 2026-09-22 on prod: 0 of 291 jobs have ever had boosted_at or boost_expires_at set, and 0 profiles have boost_credit_used_month — the free and Elite branches stamp the job inside this function and the paid branch stamps it in stripe-webhook checkoutSessionCompleted, so all three paths land on this column and none has ever fired

create-bgc-payment.why: A paid check advances the profile's verification state

check-pro-subscription.why: Column right, attribution weak: this function and stripe-webhook write the same columns and nothing records which wrote. Measured 2026-09-22 on prod: exactly 1 profile holds a tier (pro, expires 2026-10-04) and it is is_seed=true; all 5 non-seed profiles have subscription_tier NULL, so no real user has ever held a tier by any path

expire-subscriptions.observable: notifications.title='Membership expired' for the downgrade; cron.job_run_details for invocation
expire-subscriptions.why: Guess wrong — there is no expiry-reason column; the downgrade is an untagged subscription_tier=NULL write, and its one attributable trace is the notification it inserts. Measured 2026-09-22 on prod: pg_cron enqueued it 8 times, 6 succeeded, last good 2026-09-21 08:09Z (2026-09-22 failed 'job startup timeout'), while 0 'Membership expired' notifications exist — the cron runs; its downgrade branch has never had a row to clear

subscription-reconciliation.observable: cron.job_run_details for jobname='subscription-reconciliation' (a clean run writes NO product row)
subscription-reconciliation.why: Guess wrong — this function never writes error_logs: it repairs profiles, posts a Slack ops alert and returns cronResult, so a clean run leaves no durable DB trace and the only durable observable is the pg_cron enqueue record. Measured 2026-09-22 on prod: 8 enqueues, 7 succeeded, last good 2026-09-21 08:24Z (2026-09-22 'job startup timeout'); net._http_response holds no matching bodies, so response-level proof has aged out

stripe-payouts.why: Shares the transfer ledger with the release path

void-cancelled-payments.why: Guess named the wrong value: Part A's 'cancelled'/'refunded' are also written by refund and cancellation paths, so neither attributes. 'abandoned' is written in exactly ONE place in the repo (void-cancelled-payments/index.ts:466); every other mention is a read predicate. Measured 2026-09-22 on prod: 117 jobs sit at payment_status='abandoned' and ONE is is_seed=false (995fe75b, created 2026-09-21 17:19Z), so the sweep has fired on a real job, not only fixtures. cron.job_run_details corroborates: 180 retained runs, 172 succeeded, last 2026-09-22 16:10Z; that table only retains back to 2026-09-15, so the count is a floor

payment-confirm-reminder.why: Guess WRONG: this function sends no email - it inserts a notifications row (index.ts:250) and stamps jobs.payment_confirm_notif_sent (index.ts:293), so email_send_log could never show it. That stamp is written nowhere else in the repo and is the one attributable trace (the notification itself is indistinguishable from other 'job_updates' rows). Measured 2026-09-22 on prod: exactly 1 job has ever been stamped and it is is_seed=true; all 5 non-seed jobs are NULL, so no real poster has ever got this reminder. Cron alive: 30 retained runs, all succeeded, last 2026-09-22 12:15Z

instant-job-match.observable: notifications type='job_match' AND title LIKE '% Match for you%' (link '/dashboard?quickApply=<id>'), plus match_digest_queue rows
instant-job-match.why: Guess too loose: type='job_match' is NOT attributable - the notify_matching_helpers DB trigger and daily-match-digest write the same type. This function's rows are identifiable by the title it composes ('<emoji> Match for you') and the '/dashboard?quickApply=' link (index.ts:312-322), and its deferred branch upserts match_digest_queue (index.ts:330). Measured 2026-09-22 on prod: 117 job_match notifications exist (2026-09-07..2026-09-20) and ZERO carry either shape; match_digest_queue has 0 rows ever. It is also not a cron and has no invoker - no functions.invoke('instant-job-match') anywhere in src/ or supabase/, only test files reference it

email-unsubscribe.why: An unsubscribe writes a suppression row
